subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: The vertices of △ABC are A(1, 4, 2), B(−2, 1, 2) and C(2, 3, −4). Find ∠A, ∠B and ∠C.

mark_split.label: Write the direction ratios at each vertex

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), chapter 6 DIRECTION COSINES AND DIRECTION RATIOS, Long Answer question 5, book p.181. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the volume prints a chapter-level marks banner over this section but no per-step allocation on any answer. The even 2+2+2+2 split rewards the four moves the answer actually takes — the six sets of direction ratios once, then one angle each — because the three angle calculations are the same length and none of them is harder than the others. recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say which direction ratios you write at each vertex, which formula gives each angle, and how you check the three answers at the end.

steps.label: Write the direction ratios at each vertex
steps.margin_note: First two marks. An angle of the triangle is the angle between the two sides that leave that vertex, so at each vertex subtract the vertex itself from the other two points. Write all six sets before starting any angle.
steps.memory_tip: Always subtract the vertex you are standing at: the d.r's of AB are B − A, not A − B.
lines: ∠A is between the sides AB and AC:
∠B is between the sides BA and BC:
∠C is between the sides CA and CB:

recall.must_convey: That at each vertex the direction ratios of the two sides leaving it are written by subtracting that vertex from the other two points.
accept: at each vertex take the two sides that leave it
the direction ratios of A B are B minus A
subtract the vertex from the other two points
prathi vertex daggara rendu sides ki d r's rayali
write all six sets of direction ratios first
reject: apply the cosine formula to the two sets

steps.why: The angle at a vertex is the angle between the two rays that leave it, so both sets of direction ratios must point away from that vertex. Reversing one of them would give the supplement of the angle wanted.
common_mistakes: Using AB and BC for ∠A, which are not both at A.
Subtracting the other point from the vertex instead of the vertex from the other point.

steps.label: Find ∠A
steps.margin_note: Two marks. The top of the fraction comes out as 0, so the angle is a right angle and the roots underneath never have to be worked out. Say so at once.
steps.memory_tip: A zero on the top means a right angle — stop there, the bottom cannot change it.
lines: At A take (a₁, b₁, c₁) = (−3, −3, 0) and

recall.must_convey: That the sum a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ + c₁c₂ at A is 0, so cos A = 0 and ∠A = 90°.
accept: the sum of the products at A comes to zero
cos A is zero so angle A is ninety degrees
minus three plus three plus zero is zero
A daggara sum zero vasthundi kabatti ninety degrees
the two sides at A are perpendicular
reject: write the direction ratios at each vertex
cos B is three root seven by fourteen
heard_as: a one a two plus b one b two

steps.why: The sign is kept here and no modulus is used, because an interior angle of a triangle can be obtuse and a modulus would report its acute partner instead. In this triangle all three sums turn out to be zero or positive, so all three angles are right or acute.
common_mistakes: Putting a modulus on the top line — a triangle's own angle can be obtuse, so the sign is kept.
Reading a zero numerator as an angle of 0°; a zero dot product means 90°.

steps.label: Find ∠B
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Both roots simplify: √18 = 3√2 and √56 = 2√14. Rationalise the denominator so the answer reads 3√7/14.
lines: At B take (a₁, b₁, c₁) = (3, 3, 0) and

recall.must_convey: That at B the sum is 18 and the two lengths are 3√2 and 2√14, giving cos B = 3√7/14.
accept: the sum of the products at B is eighteen
the two lengths are three root two and two root fourteen
cos B is three root seven by fourteen
B daggara cos value three root seven by fourteen
rationalise the denominator to get root seven on top
reject: cos A is zero so angle A is ninety degrees
the sum at C is thirty eight

steps.why: Rationalising is what makes ∠B and ∠C comparable at the end: both cosines then sit over 14, and the check reads straight off the two answers.
common_mistakes: Leaving √28 unsimplified and never reaching the 3√7/14 form.
Giving a decimal value instead of the inverse cosine.

steps.label: Find ∠C and check the sum
steps.margin_note: The last two marks. ∠C comes out as the complement of ∠B, which is exactly what a right angle at A forces. Write that check on the page — it is the natural test that all three answers are right.
steps.memory_tip: ∠A is 90°, so ∠B and ∠C must add to 90°: check that cos C equals sin B.
lines: At C take (a₁, b₁, c₁) = (−1, 1, 6) and

recall.must_convey: That cos C = √133/14, and that the three angles are checked to add to 180° because cos C equals sin B.
accept: the sum of the products at C is thirty eight
cos C is root one hundred thirty three by fourteen
cos C equals sin B so angle C is ninety minus angle B
moodu angles kalipithe nooru enabhai degrees ravali
the three angles add to one hundred and eighty degrees
reject: cos B is three root seven by fourteen
heard_as: root one three three by fourteen

steps.why: The three angles of any triangle add to 180°, so the sum is a real test of the working and not an extra line. Here it closes exactly, because cos C equals sin B and ∠A is a right angle.
common_mistakes: Stopping after ∠C without checking that the three angles add to 180°.
Losing the factor 2 when simplifying √532 to 2√133.
